incorrect.reason: “乘龙” (Chéng Lóng) literally means 'Riding Dragon' and is a descriptive name for the Pokémon Lapras in some Chinese translations, rather than a direct phonetic translation of 'Lapras'.
“烈火” (Liè Huǒ) means 'Blazing Fire' or 'Intense Fire'. It is not a translation of 'Rapidash'.

“穿山” (Chuān Shān) literally means 'pierce mountain' or 'pangolin' (as in 穿山甲). It is part of the Chinese name for Sandslash (穿山王 'Pangolin King'), but it is not the full or direct name for 'Sandslash'.
“阿伯蛇” (Ā Bó Shé) literally means 'Arbok Snake' or 'Abok Snake'. While Arbok is a snake, this is not the official or direct Chinese translation for the Pokémon 'Arbok'.
“比雕” (Bǐ Diāo) is the Chinese name for the Pokémon 'Pidgeot', which is the evolution of Pidgeotto. It is not 'Pidgeotto'.
“铁壳昆” (Tiě Ké Kūn) means 'Iron Shell Insect'. While Kakuna is an insect, its official Chinese name uses '蛹' (yǒng, pupa), making '铁壳昆' an inaccurate translation for 'Kakuna'.
“妖精属性” (Yāo Jīng Shǔ Xìng) means 'Fairy Type' or 'Fairy Attribute'. It refers to the type, not the 'Fairy' creature or concept itself.
“磨砺” (Mó Lì) means 'to temper oneself' or 'to hone/sharpen' (skills, not physical claws). It is a more general term and not a direct translation of 'Hone Claws'.
“勇鸟猛攻” (Yǒng Niǎo Měng Gōng) means 'Brave Bird Fierce Attack' or 'Brave Bird Assault'. While it is the full name of the move, it is not a direct translation of just 'Brave Bird'.
“天王” (Tiān Wáng) literally means 'Heavenly King' and in Pokémon specifically refers to a member of the 'Elite Four'. It is not a general translation for 'Elite'.

“成都” (Chéng Dū) is the name of a major city in China. While phonetically similar to the Chinese translation for 'Johto' (城都), it uses different characters and refers to a real-world location, not the fictional 'Johto' region.
“道馆级” (Dào Guǎn Jí) means 'Gym Level' or 'Gym Grade'. It refers to a rank or level, not a 'Gym Leader' (a person).
“道馆训练家” (Dào Guǎn Xùn Liàn Jiā) means 'Gym Trainer'. While a Gym Leader is a type of Gym Trainer, it is not a direct translation of 'Gym Leader', which implies a position of authority ('Leader').
“准天王” (Zhǔn Tiān Wáng) means 'Quasi-Elite Four Member' or 'Pre-Elite Four Level'. It refers to someone who is *almost* Elite Four level, not the 'Elite Four' group itself.
“准天王资质” (Zhǔn Tiān Wáng Zī Zhì) means 'Quasi-Elite Four Aptitude' or 'Pre-Elite Four Qualification'. It refers to potential or qualification, not the 'Pre-Elite Four-Level' itself.
“水跃鱼的蛋” (Shuǐ Yuè Yú De Dàn) means 'Mudkip's Egg'. '水跃鱼' (Shuǐ Yuè Yú) is the Chinese name for Mudkip, not Magikarp.
“水跃鱼蛋” (Shuǐ Yuè Yú Dàn) means 'Mudkip Egg'. '水跃鱼' (Shuǐ Yuè Yú) is the Chinese name for Mudkip, not Magikarp.
“毒液冲击” (Dú Yè Chōng Jī) means 'Venom Shock' or 'Poison Liquid Impact'. This is the Chinese name for the Pokémon move 'Venoshock', not 'Poison Sting'.
